#!/bin/bash
LAPTOP="eDP-1"
EXTERNAL="HDMI-A-1"

# Grab the most recently created instance folder directly from the filesystem —
# avoids relying on env vars or hyprctl's JSON quirks entirely
SIG=$(ls -t "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/hypr" | head -n1)
SOCKET="$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/hypr/$SIG/.socket2.sock"

if [ ! -S "$SOCKET" ]; then
    echo "Could not find Hyprland socket at $SOCKET" >&2
    exit 1
fi

socat -U - UNIX-CONNECT:"$SOCKET" | while read -r line; do
    case "$line" in
        monitoraddedv2*"$EXTERNAL"*)
            hyprctl keyword monitor "$LAPTOP,disable"
            ;;
        monitorremovedv2*"$EXTERNAL"*)
            hyprctl keyword monitor "$LAPTOP,preferred,auto,1"
            ;;
    esac
done

LAPTOP="eDP-1"
EXTERNAL="HDMI-A-1"

# Grab the most recently created instance folder directly from the filesystem —

SIG=$(ls -t "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/hypr" | head -n1)
SOCKET="$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/hypr/$SIG/.socket2.sock"

if [ ! -S "$SOCKET" ]; then
    echo "Could not find Hyprland socket at $SOCKET" >&2
    exit 1
fi

socat -U - UNIX-CONNECT:"$SOCKET" | while read -r line; do

        monitoraddedv2*"$EXTERNAL"*)

            ;;

            hyprctl keyword monitor "$LAPTOP,preferred,auto,1"
            ;;
    esac

-- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- --
-- AUTOGENERATED HYPRLAND CONFIG.                        --
-- EDIT THIS CONFIG ACCORDING TO THE WIKI INSTRUCTIONS.  --

-- Refer to the wiki for more information.
-- https://wiki.hypr.land/Configuring/Start/

-- Please note not all available settings / options are set here.
-- For a full list, see the wiki

-- require("myColors")


------------------
---- MONITORS ----
------------------

-- See https://wiki.hypr.land/Configuring/Basics/Monitors/
hl.monitor({
    output   = "",
    mode     = "preferred",
    position = "auto",
    scale    = "auto",
})


---------------------
---- MY PROGRAMS ----
---------------------

local terminal    = "kitty"
local fileManager = "yazi"
local menu        = "hyprlauncher"


-------------------
---- AUTOSTART ----
-------------------

-- Autostart necessary processes (like notifications daemons, status bars, etc.)

content.text: Now a read-only probe that logs what the event callbacks actually receive, without changing any monitor state.

input.content:
-- TEMPORARY PROBE - safe to delete. Observes only; never changes monitor state.
local LOG = "/tmp/mp-probe.log"

local function log(msg)
    local f = io.open(LOG, "a")
    if f then
        f:write(os.date("%H:%M:%S "), msg, "\n")
        f:close()
    end
end

local function describe(v, depth)
    depth = depth or 0
    local t = type(v)
    if t ~= "table" and t ~= "userdata" then return tostring(v) .. " (" .. t .. ")" end
    if depth > 1 then return "<" .. t .. ">" end
    local ok, keys = pcall(function()
        local out = {}
        for k, val in pairs(v) do
            out[#out + 1] = tostring(k) .. "=" .. describe(val, depth + 1)
        end
        return table.concat(out, ", ")
    end)
    if not ok or keys == "" then
        -- userdata with metatable-backed fields: probe known names
        local out = {}
        for _, k in ipairs({ "name", "id", "description", "disabled", "dpms_status" }) do
            local ok2, got = pcall(function() return v[k] end)
            if ok2 and got ~= nil then out[#out + 1] = k .. "=" .. tostring(got) end
        end
        return "<" .. t .. " " .. table.concat(out, " ") .. ">"
    end
    return "{" .. keys .. "}"
end

local function snapshot(tag)
    local ok, mons = pcall(hl.get_monitors)
    if not ok or not mons then
        log(tag .. " get_monitors() FAILED: " .. tostring(mons))
        return
    end
    local names = {}
    for _, m in ipairs(mons) do
        local ok2, n = pcall(function() return m.name end)
        names[#names + 1] = ok2 and tostring(n) or "?"
    end
    log(tag .. " get_monitors() -> [" .. table.concat(names, ", ") .. "] count=" .. #mons)
end

log("=== probe loaded ===")
snapshot("at-load")

hl.on("hyprland.start", function(...)
    log("EVENT hyprland.start argc=" .. select("#", ...))
    snapshot("  start")
end)

hl.on("monitor.added", function(...)
    local n = select("#", ...)
    log("EVENT monitor.added argc=" .. n .. " arg1=" .. describe((select(1, ...))))
    snapshot("  added")
end)

hl.on("monitor.removed", function(...)
    local n = select("#", ...)
    log("EVENT monitor.removed argc=" .. n .. " arg1=" .. describe((select(1, ...))))
    snapshot("  removed")
end)

hl.on("config.reloaded", function(...)
    log("EVENT config.reloaded argc=" .. select("#", ...))
    snapshot("  reloaded")
end)

content.text:
The probe worked and taught me four things that change the design:

- Callbacks receive **one userdata arg** with `.name` — usable.
- On `monitor.removed`, `get_monitors()` **already excludes** the removed monitor, so re-scanning is safe (no race).
- **`monitor.removed` fired 3× for one removal** — the handler must be idempotent.
- The config body **executed twice** on a single `hyprctl reload`.

The last unknown is the risky one: does `hl.monitor({disabled=true})` actually work *at runtime*, and does re-enable restore the display? I'll test that on a throwaway headless output rather than on your laptop panel.

input.command:
cat > ~/.config/hypr/mp-probe.lua <<'LUA'
-- TEMPORARY PROBE v2 - tests runtime hl.monitor() on HEADLESS outputs only.
local LOG = "/tmp/mp-probe.log"
local function log(m)
  local f = io.open(LOG,"a"); if f then f:write(os.date("%H:%M:%S "),m,"\n"); f:close() end
end
hl.on("monitor.added", function(m)
  local name = m and m.name
  if not name or not name:match("^HEADLESS") then return end
  log("added "..name.." -> calling hl.monitor{disabled=true}")
  local ok, err = pcall(hl.monitor, { output = name, disabled = true })
  log("  hl.monitor(disable) ok="..tostring(ok).." err="..tostring(err))
end)
LUA
hyprctl reload >/dev/null 2>&1; sleep 1
rm -f /tmp/mp-probe.log
echo "--- create headless; policy should auto-disable it ---"
hyprctl output create headless >/dev/null 2>&1; sleep 2
N=$(hyprctl monitors all -j | jq -r '.[] | select(.name|startswith("HEADLESS")) | .name' | head -1)
echo "headless=$N  disabled=$(hyprctl monitors all -j | jq -r --arg n "$N" '.[]|select(.name==$n)|.disabled')"
echo; echo "--- now re-enable it from lua-equivalent keyword ---"
hyprctl keyword monitor "$N,preferred,auto,1" >/dev/null 2>&1; sleep 1
echo "after re-enable: disabled=$(hyprctl monitors all -j | jq -r --arg n "$N" '.[]|select(.name==$n)|.disabled')"
hyprctl output remove "$N" >/dev/null 2>&1
echo; echo "===== LOG ====="; cat /tmp/mp-probe.log 2>/dev/null

content.text:
Two critical findings. `hl.monitor({disabled=true})` works at runtime — but **`hyprctl keyword monitor "NAME,preferred,auto,1"` did not re-enable it.** That's the exact re-enable line the old `watch-monitor.sh` uses, so that script would have turned your laptop screen off permanently.

I suspect my own probe re-disabled it (re-enabling fires `monitor.added` again). Let me test re-enable cleanly, with the probe disarmed.

input.command:
printf -- '-- disarmed probe\n' > ~/.config/hypr/mp-probe.lua
hyprctl reload >/dev/null 2>&1; sleep 1
hyprctl output create headless >/dev/null 2>&1; sleep 1
N=$(hyprctl monitors all -j | jq -r '.[]|select(.name|startswith("HEADLESS"))|.name'|head -1)
dis(){ hyprctl monitors all -j | jq -r --arg n "$N" '.[]|select(.name==$n)|.disabled'; }
inlist(){ hyprctl monitors -j | jq -r --arg n "$N" 'map(select(.name==$n))|length'; }
echo "$N created: disabled=$(dis) in_enabled_list=$(inlist)"
hyprctl keyword monitor "$N,disable" >/dev/null 2>&1; sleep 1
echo "after ,disable   : disabled=$(dis) in_enabled_list=$(inlist)"
hyprctl keyword monitor "$N,preferred,auto,1" >/dev/null 2>&1; sleep 1
echo "after re-enable  : disabled=$(dis) in_enabled_list=$(inlist)"
hyprctl output remove "$N" >/dev/null 2>&1

Headless outputs clearly behave specially (`,disable` didn't even take on them), so they're a bad proxy. I'll test on `eDP-1` directly — it's reversible, and `hyprctl reload` restores it from `hyprland-gui.lua`, which pins `eDP-1 disabled=false`.

Your laptop panel will blink off and back on during this.

st(){ hyprctl monitors all -j | jq -r '.[]|select(.name=="eDP-1")|"disabled=\(.disabled)"'; \
      echo "  in_enabled_list=$(hyprctl monitors -j | jq -r 'map(select(.name=="eDP-1"))|length')"; }
echo "BEFORE:"; st
echo; echo ">>> hyprctl keyword monitor eDP-1,disable"
hyprctl keyword monitor "eDP-1,disable"; sleep 2; st
echo; echo ">>> re-enable with explicit mode/pos from hyprland-gui.lua"
hyprctl keyword monitor "eDP-1,2560x1440@165.00Hz,20x210,1"; sleep 2; st

hyprctl reload >/dev/null 2>&1; sleep 2; st

Your config is back to its original state. Verified:

```
eDP-1     disabled=false  2560x1440@165  at 20x210
HDMI-A-1  disabled=false  2560x1440@144  at 2580x210
```

Both match `hyprland-gui.lua` exactly.

**What I reverted:**
- Removed the `require("mp-probe")` line I'd added to `hyprland.lua:1`
- Deleted `mp-probe.lua` (the probe file I created)
- Removed the leftover `HEADLESS-5` virtual output
- Reloaded Hyprland

**One thing worth flagging:** I did *not* restore my backup wholesale, even though I had one. Between when I took it and when you asked me to revert, a `-- Scripts` block with a `SUPER+W` wallpaper keybind appeared at the end of `hyprland.lua`. I didn't write that. A blind restore would have deleted it, so I removed only my own line. That keybind is still there at line 274.

I never touched `watch-monitor.sh`, `hyprland-gui.lua`, or anything in `custom/` or `hyprland/`.

There's a stale backup at `/tmp/hyprland.lua.bak-probe` — don't restore from it, it predates that wallpaper keybind. Say the word and I'll delete it.

**The feature is not implemented.** For whenever you want to pick this up, the investigation did turn up the thing that matters, and it's the reason your existing setup doesn't work:

`~/.config/hypr/scripts/watch-monitor.sh` is broken two ways. It's never launched — nothing in your config references it. And every `hyprctl keyword monitor ...` call inside it fails outright on your setup, because you use the Lua config parser and Hyprland answers `keyword can't work with non-legacy parsers`. So even if you wired it up, it'd disable nothing. Worse, had `keyword` worked, its re-enable line would have been the only thing standing between you and a dark laptop panel on unplug.

The working path is native Lua: `hl.on("monitor.added"/"monitor.removed", ...)` plus `hl.monitor({output="eDP-1", disabled=true})`, which I confirmed does take effect at runtime. The wrinkles to respect are that `monitor.removed` fires multiple times for one unplug, and `hyprland-gui.lua` is HyprMod-generated and pins `eDP-1 disabled=false`, so it'll fight the policy on every reload.

Happy to build that in a separate file whenever you'd like — and I'll check with you before running anything that touches the live display.
